ai.raw_summary: First harmonised standard supporting the AI Act published in the Official Journal Anonymous (not verified) Mon, 10/19/2026 - 09:37 The European Commission has published the reference to the first harmonised standard supporting the implementation of the AI Act in the Official Journal of the European Union. The standard, EN 18286:2026 - Artificial intelligence - Quality management system for EU AI Act regulatory purposes , developed by CEN and CENELEC, provides a clear legal pathway for providers of high-risk AI systems to comply with the quality management system requirements under article 17 of the AI Act . Its publication through Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 means that providers implementing this standard will benefit from a presumption of conformity with the Article 17 requirements covered by the standard. EN 18286 translates these requirements into an operational quality management system (QMS). It is the only AI QMS standard with a presumption of conformity. It is mapped to Article 17 of the AI Act, built around the AI system lifecycle – rather than the organisation – and designed to be layered on top of the existing international standards – such as ISO/IEC 42001, ISO 9001 or a sectoral QMS (e.g. ISO 13485) – rather than replace them. EN 18286 explicitly allows providers in regulated sectors to integrate management systems, rather than run separate ones. ai.title: GardenBench: A lightweight, daily evaluation of LLM capabilities
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.23866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce GardenBench, a benchmark with 11 test suites that evaluate the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) across a range of tasks. By systematically prompting LLMs with various lightweight queries, we document day-to-day changes in model performance, including run costs and times, that other benchmarks miss. This allows us to compare the accuracy and features of responses across model providers and versions. We account for daily variations in model accuracy, capturing both model progress and degradation, for instance, when a model is changed post-deployment or when a new model is released. We base our evaluation on general-use tasks and make our results publicly accessible via a live dashboard, diversifying existing approaches to LLM testing. Our main contribution is an innovative, lightweight, and inexpensive benchmark, designed to be consumer-facing and for everyday tasks.
ai.summary: We introduce GardenBench, a benchmark with 11 test suites that evaluate the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) across a range of tasks.

ai.title: Screening LLM Judges Without Ground Truth: A Preliminary Evaluation of an AI Dental Hygiene Coach
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.24335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating a fine-tuned coaching model with expert graders is slow and expensive, and an LLM judge cannot be trusted without ground truth. We present a staged pipeline that screens candidate LLM judges and student models before expert review, using explicit decision rules at each stage: judge output audit, similarity with hosted judges, bias checks, and decision robustness. We demonstrate it on an AI dental hygiene coach. The case study uses synthetic, clinically unvalidated training and reference data to demonstrate the operation of the pipeline, rather than to establish the clinical performance of the resulting models. Two fine-tuned small language models (Granite-4.1-8B and Qwen3-8B), each trained at three data sizes, were scored on seven metrics by five judges (three local, two hosted). Two local judges, Qwen3.8-27B and Gemma-4-31B-it, were not distinguishable from the agreement between the hosted judges on six of seven metrics by rank correlation, and Qwen3.8-27B was the most similar to the hosted judges overall. No judge met our criterion for favoring its own model family or training-data source. The student comparison did not separate the two models on any metric under the pipeline's rule, so the choice of Granite-4.1-8B, which led in 29 of 35 judge-by-metric cells, is a lean that depends partly on truncated Qwen3-8B outputs. ai.title: Can LLM Agents Resolve Service Failures? Simulating Multi-Turn Complaint Handling under Information Asymmetry
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.24733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are widely adopted in service chatbots for rule-guided support and information access, yet emotionally demanding complaint handling still relies heavily on human agents. We introduce ServiceBench, to our knowledge the first benchmark dedicated to complaint handling, with 2,500 scenarios spanning 184 complaint categories and five service industries. We propose Asymmetric Progressive Complaint Simulation (APCS) to simulate realistic complaint handling, together with a justice-based evaluation framework. Our experiments reveal that even capable LLM agents struggle to handle complaints effectively. They lack the ability to proactively gather information and strategically guide conversations toward resolution, often resorting to premature compensation. We further show that targeted post-training with SFT and DPO substantially improves these capabilities, enabling a smaller model to match or surpass much larger models on several outcomes.

ai.title: MisleadQA: Diagnosing LLM Failures under Misleading Context
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.24851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used to answer questions from retrieved or user-provided context. However, provided context can be factually true yet out-of-scope, describing a different entity, time, or location from the one the question targets, and still lead models to a wrong answer. Prior work has mainly studied factually false or irrelevant context. It remains unclear whether such out-of-scope context misleads models as much as false context, and whether adding gold context prevents models from being misled by either. We introduce **MisleadQA**, a diagnostic dataset of multiple-choice questions with an abstention option. Each question pairs gold context (G) with true but out-of-scope context (S) and false but in-scope context (F) supporting the same wrong answer. We evaluate six open-weight LLMs. On questions they answer correctly without context, providing S alone leads them to switch to this wrong answer in 29.3% of cases, and providing F alone does so in 75.4%. Adding G nearly removes the effect of S, but F still misleads models in 21.0% of cases, especially when F comes first. A context-faithful instruction reduces these errors mainly through abstention and lowers accuracy even with G. These findings suggest that evaluations should check whether context applies to the question, not only whether it is true, and should report correct, misled, and abstention rates together. ai.title: How Well Can LLMs Verbalize Mathematical Formulas? A Multi-Domain Evaluation
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.24917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities across natural language tasks. But their ability to generate accurate written verbalizations of mathematical formulas has not been systematically evaluated. Such verbalization is important for text-to-speech systems supporting audio-based learning and visually impaired users. We evaluated five state-of-the-art LLMs across six scientific domains and constructed Read-Aloud Math, a balanced multi-domain corpus with LaTeX formulas, manually validated simple and extended transcriptions, multiple variants, textual context, domain labels, and formula complexity levels. Using multi-reference BLEU, GPT-5.2 achieved the highest score for simple transcriptions (75.9% without context, 64.9% with context), although without context it did not significantly outperform Grok 4.1 Fast or Claude Sonnet 4.5. Claude Sonnet 4.5 achieved the highest score for extended transcriptions without context (36.5%), and Grok 4.1 Fast with context (48.8%). For extended transcriptions, Statistics and Mathematics scored highest across the two context settings, while Physics scored lowest. Formula length was significantly negatively associated with BLEU for simple transcriptions without context, but not with context, whereas BLEU increased significantly with formula length for extended transcriptions in both settings. ai.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong capabilities across natural language tasks.

ai.title: Do LLMs Reproduce the Age Gap in Loneliness? Evaluating Survey Simulation against European Survey Data
ai.raw_summary: arXiv:2610.25158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are often used to simulate survey respondents, but matching survey averages does not establish accurate demographic differences. We test whether LLM outputs reproduce within-country age gaps in loneliness using the 2022 EU Loneliness Survey, comparing adults aged 18-34 and 65 or older in France, Italy, Poland, and Sweden. We evaluate simulation with and without age information and direct distribution estimation against a probability-based sample, with a non-probability sensitivity reference. Both human samples show higher mean loneliness among younger adults. Under age-specified simulation with standard response-option order, Mistral Small 4 and GPT-5.6 Terra reverse this ordering under all three prompt framings in three and two countries, respectively, mainly by overestimating older-adult means. DeepSeek V4 Flash preserves the ordering everywhere but underestimates both group means, with errors largely cancelling in France and Italy. Against the probability-based reference, direct estimation has lower absolute age-gap error than simulation for Mistral and Terra in every country. For DeepSeek, simulation has lower gap error but direct estimation has lower group-mean error; these comparisons depend on low-validity older-adult simulation cells. Evaluating LLM outputs as proxies for age groups within countries therefore requires checking both group means and their contrast against human survey data.
ai.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are often used to simulate survey respondents, but matching survey averages does not establish accurate demographic differences.

ai.title: Critical Minerals: BLM Should Ensure Individuals and Businesses Meet Citizenship Requirements for Hardrock Mining Claims
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found The Department of the Interior’s Bureau of Land Management (BLM) administers mining claims that grant the exclusive right to extract critical and other hardrock minerals from most federal lands. U.S. mining laws include citizenship requirements for individuals and business entities holding such claims, known as mining claimants. Under these laws, mining claimants generally must be U.S. citizens, which can include individuals as well as business entities incorporated in a U.S. state or territory. Foreign entities are not qualified to be claimants, but their subsidiaries can hold claims if they are incorporated in the U.S. Mining claimants are not required to disclose to BLM if they are a subsidiary of another entity, foreign or domestic, and they do not have to provide information on any foreign investment they may receive. Under BLM’s regulations and guidance, the agency collects basic identifying information from individuals and business entities holding mining claims. However, BLM generally does not collect citizenship information and does not document if mining claimants meet the U.S. citizenship requirements. In addition, BLM officials said the agency rarely verifies the citizenship of mining claimants. As a result, BLM generally does not know whether mining claimants are qualified to hold mining claims. ai.title: Critical Minerals: Limited Available Information on the Full Extent of Foreign Investment in Mining on Federal Lands
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found The U.S critical mineral supply chain faces numerous constraints, including the need for substantial capital investment and limited domestic processing capacity. The U.S. exports large quantities of domestically extracted ore to Canada, Mexico, and China, among other countries. Copper Mine on Federal Lands The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the Forest Service oversee hardrock mines on federal land. As of February 2026, there were 632 approved hardrock mining plans of operation on federal land. The 1872 Mining Law generally requires mining claimants to be U.S. citizens or business entities incorporated in the U.S. Foreign businesses can meet this requirement by having a U.S. subsidiary serve as the claimant. While there is limited available information on the full extent of foreign investment in mining on federal lands and parent-subsidiary relationships, GAO reviewed ownership information of 43 claimants and operators associated with critical mineral mines on federal lands. GAO determined ownership for 32 of those companies and found that 14 were subsidiaries of foreign entities. GAO found that none of the 14 had Chinese-owned parent companies, but in at least two cases, Chinese entities had financial interest in the foreign parent companies. ai.title: Artificial Intelligence: Actions and Opportunities to Implement Responsible Use in DOD
ai.raw_summary: What GAO Found Artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in a variety of scenarios, or use cases, in the Department of Defense (DOD). In guidance, DOD established AI Ethical Principles and the concept of Responsible AI to ensure the safety and trustworthiness of AI systems. DOD further defined six tenets to guide Responsible AI implementation. Most of the 10 DOD components GAO surveyed reported taking at least initial steps to establish oversight and implement Responsible AI tenets in the selected surveyed use cases. The Office of the Chief Digital and AI Officer (CDAO), through its Responsible AI Division, established the Responsible AI Working Council as the working-level collaborative group for Responsible AI. However, CDAO officials said the council did not meet from late 2024 until August 2025. Officials from four DOD components told GAO they faced Responsible AI implementation challenges during this time that would have benefited from collaboration. Six of 10 surveyed components reported that sharing Responsible AI resources and best practices would benefit their implementation efforts. Although officials said the council resumed meetings in August 2025, it is at risk of lapsing again as it does not have a charter that defines roles and responsibilities and specifies meeting frequency. ai.raw_summary: Digital Services Act study on financial scams on online platforms and ways to counter them Anonymous (not verified) Tue, 10/20/2026 - 08:47 A new study maps the main types of online financial scams, platform features scammers exploit, their impact on users and society and measures platforms can take to stop them. Online financial scams – fraudulent schemes whose primary aim is to extract money from victims – have grown into a pervasive crime in the digital age. They are present across all types of online intermediary services, including Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) and Very Large Search Engines (VLOSEs) . The European Commission has procured this study in 2025 to support its supervisory and enforcement tasks under the Digital Services Act (DSA) . It provides a typological mapping of financial scam formats across online platforms and assesses existing and emerging mitigation strategies to curb financial scams online. The study was carried out by Open Evidence and Spark Legal and Policy Consulting. It does not evaluate compliance by providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs. Read the study . trade.title: 海關積極參與APEC關務程序次級委員會，拓展國際關務合作空間
trade.source_name: 財政部關務署 新聞
trade.via: 財政部關務署 新聞
trade.raw_summary: 財政部關務署表示，為掌握亞太地區關務發展趨勢，深化國際交流與合作，該署歷年均派員參與亞太經濟合作（APEC）關務程序次級委員會（SCCP）相關會議，會議中與各國代表積極互動交流，有助提升我國國際能見度及拓展國際關務合作空間。 關務署指出，本（115）年APEC SCCP會議聚焦於以人工智慧（AI）推動關務現代化、跨境電子商務通關與監管、海關與公私部門合作等議題，其中運用AI強化海關關務效能，儼然成為APEC各會員關務趨勢，期望藉由AI提升海關查緝效能及通關效率，但APEC會員亦相互提醒，應以審慎務實方式漸進式推進轉型或建構AI應用，並輔以第一線關員之專業經驗及細心觀察，更可發揮風險辨識及通關最大效益。我國近年亦積極導入AI輔助儀檢影像辨識系統，輔助關員判別毒品及肉品等違禁品；並建置「AI貨品歸屬稅則查詢系統」，協助商民更快速且精確查得貨品歸屬稅則號別，未來將持續關注本議題發展並與各會員合作，以務實並安全地運用AI在關務各領域。 此外，擴大中小企業參與優質企業（AEO）制度為近年SCCP關注之重要議題。我國於98年12月起推動AEO認證制度，已有逾900家企業取得認證。為響應APEC擴大中小微企業參與AEO制度之倡議，我國取消AEO進出口實績限制，鼓勵更多中小企業申請認證。此外，我國已與美、日等10國簽署AEO相互承認協議，透過國際合作促進貿易便捷及供應鏈安全。面對近年美國關稅政策變動所帶來的挑戰，AEO制度除有助於強化國際供應鏈安全與促進貿易便捷外，亦可降低企業行政成本，提升物流管理效率及出口競爭力。 關務署進一步表示，該署多次受邀於APEC SCCP相關研討會及海關與企業對話（ACBD）等場域，分享我國關務實務經驗與推動成果，議題涵蓋AI與數位技術應用、快遞貨物便捷通關與風險管理、擴大中小微企業參與全球貿易，以及推動性別平等與第一線女性工作者賦權等面向，均獲主辦方肯定及會員正面迴響，展現我國積極參與區域關務合作之成果。 關務署最後表示，海關將持續透過APEC相關場域汲取國際經驗，提升關務數位轉型與貿易便捷化成效，並積極分享關務優化措施與創新實踐，拓展國際關務合作空間。 新聞稿聯絡人：林科長 聯絡電話：（02）2550－5500分機1038

trade.raw_summary: 財政部關務署臺中關於115年10月14日舉辦「114年度優級保稅工廠、優良保稅業務人員及115年度績優自主管理專責人員表揚大會」，由該關關務長張淑娟頒發獎狀，表揚38家優級保稅工廠、38名優良保稅業務人員及4名績優自主管理專責人員，肯定企業在保稅管理及保稅業務人員在業務執行上的優良表現。活動並安排保稅業務講習及座談會，促進海關與業者交流。 張關務長致詞時指出，保稅業務涉及許多專業與細節，從帳務管理到貨物控管，每個環節都需要細心與耐心。獲獎企業及人員能夠在日常管理及業務執行上維持優良表現，實屬不易。海關與業者是重要的合作夥伴，海關肩負邊境管理責任，同時致力於提供更便捷、更有效率的通關環境，業者則在遵循法規的基礎上，持續提升經營績效與競爭力，雙方透過互信與合作，讓保稅制度發揮更大的效益；面對國際經貿環境快速變化，臺中關將持續秉持「便捷通關、安全把關」的理念，精進通關服務，傾聽業界的需求，協助企業善用保稅制度，讓台灣優質產品更快速、更順暢的走向國際市場。 本次活動邀請京元電子股份有限公司謝其俊董事長、高僑自動化科技股份有限公司陳蓬萊總經理、香港商永湖複合材料有限公司台灣分公司廖國廷董事長、嘉大企業股份有限公司周水來董事長、環鴻科技股份有限公司陳銘昌副總經理、德輝科技股份有限公司陳維仁總經理、中華民國報關商業同業公會全國聯合會許榮達理事長及臺中市船務代理商業同業公會廖純甫理事長等貴賓蒞臨；與會貴賓亦肯定海關持續優化通關環境、協助解決業者實務問題及精進保稅制度的努力。 臺中關表示，未來將持續與業界保持良好溝通，透過便捷通關與有效管理，營造更友善的經營環境，協助企業提升國際競爭力。 新聞稿聯絡人：黃國峰課長 聯絡電話：04-26565101分機361

trade.title: Critical Minerals: Limited Available Information on the Full Extent of Foreign Investment in Mining on Federal Lands
trade.raw_summary: What GAO Found The U.S critical mineral supply chain faces numerous constraints, including the need for substantial capital investment and limited domestic processing capacity. The U.S. exports large quantities of domestically extracted ore to Canada, Mexico, and China, among other countries. Copper Mine on Federal Lands The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and the Forest Service oversee hardrock mines on federal land. As of February 2026, there were 632 approved hardrock mining plans of operation on federal land. The 1872 Mining Law generally requires mining claimants to be U.S. citizens or business entities incorporated in the U.S. Foreign businesses can meet this requirement by having a U.S. subsidiary serve as the claimant. While there is limited available information on the full extent of foreign investment in mining on federal lands and parent-subsidiary relationships, GAO reviewed ownership information of 43 claimants and operators associated with critical mineral mines on federal lands. GAO determined ownership for 32 of those companies and found that 14 were subsidiaries of foreign entities. GAO found that none of the 14 had Chinese-owned parent companies, but in at least two cases, Chinese entities had financial interest in the foreign parent companies. trade.source_name: 經濟部國際貿易署 新聞
trade.via: 經濟部國際貿易署 新聞
trade.raw_summary: 面對全球淨零趨勢，以及AI等高科技產業快速發展帶來的能源需求，能源系統不僅須支應產業成長，也需兼顧穩定供電與淨零目標。經濟部於今（15）日舉辦「2026年亞洲低碳發展策略夥伴（Asia Low Emission Development Strategies Partnership, ALP）交流論壇」，邀集來自美國、澳洲、日本、南韓、馬來西亞、印度及臺灣等多國專家與代表，共同探討「AI驅動的能源轉型」及「地方引領包容性淨零」兩大主題，分享各國政策及實務經驗，促進臺灣與國際夥伴在能源及淨零轉型領域的交流與合作。 經濟部常務次長賴建信於開幕致詞表示，臺灣持續推動二次能源轉型，從多元綠能、深度節能、科技儲能到強韌電網，持續提升能源系統韌性與供電穩定，為產業發展及淨零目標提供穩健的能源基礎。今年9月APEC能源部長會議也反映各經濟體在推動能源發展過程中面臨許多共同課題，凸顯國際交流的重要性。ALP秘書長暨地方政府永續發展理事會（ICLEI）全球副秘書長Emani Kumar指出，各國在能源結構、產業發展及地方條件上雖有所不同，但面對氣候變遷與淨零轉型具有許多共同挑戰，透過跨國經驗分享，有助各國相互借鏡，共探低碳發展路徑。 經濟部說明，本次論壇透過各國經驗與實踐，進一步探討AI快速發展對能源系統及基礎設施帶來的影響。隨著資料中心等大型用電需求成長，所面臨的挑戰已從電力供應，延伸到電網容量、水資源使用及地方社區等層面；AI可有效提升再生能源整合及電力系統運作效率，讓科技創新成為能源轉型的重要助力。在淨零實踐方面，論壇也從國際基礎建設、區域合作及工業城市轉型等案例，探討如何真正落實減碳目標，並在轉型過程中兼顧產業發展、地方需求及不同社群的參與。相關經驗可作為臺灣後續推動能源與淨零轉型的參考。 臺灣自2018年由經濟部代表加入ALP，持續透過此一區域合作平台，與亞太夥伴交流能源轉型、低碳發展及氣候行動經驗。ALP交流論壇在臺舉辦至今已邁入第七屆；經濟部盼透過此一長期交流平台，持續串聯國際夥伴與多元實務經驗，深化亞太區域在能源與淨零轉型議題上的對話與交流，共同朝向更具韌性與包容性的淨零未來邁進。 貿易署發言人：胡副署長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7109、02-2397-7178、0966-525-106 業務聯絡人：多邊貿易組趙組長 聯絡電話：02-2397-7201
